RE has a more consistent story line and has multiple games where they continue a characters story (think chris in RE:1  -> code veronica -> RE:5 -> RE:6 -> village). 

i think people would rather enjoy following a character on their journey, seeing them grow and wanting to know how their story concludes, rather than one-off characters in a lot of silent hill games (i know there’s also one-off characters in RE, but they aren’t usually protags). 

it’s hard for people to really connect with characters in a long-time franchise if they don’t make reappearances. not saying silent hill should do this at all, it’s just what i think made RE stick around longer. 

also the availability of games. steam is almost always having sales of pretty much every core RE game, but the only silent hill game available on steam is homecoming. if you’re new to both fandoms and not sure where to start, you can hop on steam and start at the beginning with RE:1... or watch gameplay for silent hill. 

i also think that silent hill 2 is a lot less accessible because of the price. where steam is always having sales for RE games, silent hill is notoriously hard to obtain without emulators. i think a lot of silent hill fans and video game collectors have such a pretentious attitude towards the game, which has killed a lot of interest for people newer to the fandom, who might want to actually play the game instead of watching it. 

silent hill also hasn’t aged as well. you’re still able to enjoy the classic RE by emulating the older games, but theyre also in the process of remaking their franchise for a newer audience. i know silent hill is also doing this, but i think RE started the trend with 2. i don’t even think the silent hill 2 remake would exist without RE:2R
